item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 170511
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Fri Oct 16 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Trudy, located a couple of hundred miles west-southwest of
Acapulco, Mexico.

South of Southern Mexico:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form offshore of southern
Mexico during the early to middle part of next week. Environmental
conditions appear conducive for gradual development thereafter, and
a tropical depression is likely to form during the latter half of
next week while it moves generally westward to west-northwestward
over the eastern and central portions of the East Pacific.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

$$
Forecaster Pierce/Gibbs

item.title: Hurricane Trudy Public Advisory Number 15a
item.description:
Issued at 1200 AM CST Sat Oct 17 2026 
000
WTPZ31 KNHC 170553
TCPEP1
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Trudy Intermediate Advisory Number 15A
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
1200 AM CST Sat Oct 17 2026
 
...TRUDY HOLDING STEADY...
...TRUDY FORECAST TO APPROACH THE SOUTHWESTERN AND WEST-CENTRAL
COAST OF MEXICO THIS WEEKEND...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1200 AM CST...0600 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...15.7N 103.1W
ABOUT 230 MI...365 KM WSW OF ACAPULCO MEXICO
ABOUT 240 MI...390 KM SSE OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...90 MPH...150 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NNW OR 330 DEGREES AT 7 MPH...11 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...979 MB...28.91 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Warning is in effect for...
* The coast of Mexico from Manzanillo northward to Cabo Corrientes
 
A Hurricane Watch is in effect for...
* The coast of Mexico from south of Manzanillo to Punta San Telmo
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* The coast of Mexico from south of Manzanillo to Zihuatanejo
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* The coast of Mexico north of Cabo Corrientes to San Blas
* Las Islas Marias
 
A Hurricane Warning means that hurricane conditions are expected
somewhere within the warning area. A warning is typically issued 36
hours before the anticipated first occurrence of
tropical-storm-force winds, conditions that make outside
preparations difficult or dangerous. Preparations to protect life
and property should be rushed to completion.
 
A Hurricane Watch means that hurricane conditions are possible
within the watch area. A watch is typically issued 48 hours before
the anticipated first occurrence of tropical-storm-force winds,
conditions that make outside preparations difficult or dangerous.
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area within 36 hours.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, generally within 48 hours.
 
Interests elsewhere in southwestern and west-central Mexico should
continue to monitor the progress of Trudy. Additional watches or
warnings will likely be required today.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1200 AM CST (0600 UTC), the center of Hurricane Trudy was located 
near latitude 15.7 North, longitude 103.1 West. Trudy is moving 
toward the north-northwest near 7 mph (11 km/h). A turn toward the 
northwest at a faster forward speed is expected today, and this 
general motion is forecast to continue through Sunday. On the 
forecast track, the center of Trudy will approach the coast of 
southwestern and west-central Mexico today and pass near the coast 
tonight into Sunday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 90 mph (150 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Some strengthening is possible today, followed by weakening 
beginning by Sunday.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 30 miles (45 km) from
the center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 140
miles (220 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 979 mb (28.91 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Trudy can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP1 and WMO header WTPZ41 KNHC
and on the web at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?key_messages.
 
WIND: Hurricane conditions are expected in the Hurricane Warning
area by tonight, with tropical storm conditions spreading across the
area today. Tropical storm conditions are expected within the
Tropical Storm Warning area today. Hurricane conditions are possible
in the Hurricane Watch area by late today. Tropical storm conditions
are possible in the Tropical Storm Watch area by Sunday.
 
RAINFALL: Through the weekend, Trudy is expected to produce 4 to 8
inches with isolated higher totals around 15 inches along and near
the southwest Mexican coast in Michoacán, Colima and Jalisco. This
rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides,
especially in areas along steep terrain.
 
Elsewhere, Trudy’s outer bands are expected to produce 2 to 4 inch
with isolated higher totals around 6 inches along the southwest
Mexican coast in Guerrero and Nayarit. This rainfall may result in
localized flash flooding through the weekend, especially in areas
along steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Trudy,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?rainqpf.
 
STORM SURGE: Coastal flooding from storm surge is possible in areas
of onshore winds. Near the coast, the surge will be accompanied by
large and destructive waves.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Trudy are affecting portions of the coast
of southwestern Mexico and will spread northward toward west-central
Mexico through the weekend. These swells will cause life-threatening
surf and rip current conditions. Please consult products from your
local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 AM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Gibbs

item.title: Hurricane Trudy Forecast Discussion Number 15
item.description:
Issued at 900 PM CST Fri Oct 16 2026 
003 
WTPZ41 KNHC 170240
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Trudy Discussion Number  15
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
900 PM CST Fri Oct 16 2026
 
Trudy's satellite presentation has improved somewhat this evening, 
with deep convection becoming better organized near the center and a 
possible ragged eye beginning to reappear. Cloud tops as cold as -85 
degrees C have been observed within the convective band wrapping 
into the system over the northern semicircle. The latest subjective 
Dvorak intensity estimate from TAFB is T4.5/77 kt, while recent 
objective estimates have been as high as 75 kt. Given the recent 
improvement in the satellite presentation, the initial intensity has 
been increased to 80 kt.

The initial motion is northward, or about 350/6 kt. A turn toward 
the north-northwest and then northwest at a faster forward speed is 
expected overnight and into Saturday as a weak low- to mid-level 
ridge builds over eastern Mexico. This general motion should 
continue through Sunday, bringing the center of Trudy very close 
to portions of the coast of west-central Mexico. Thereafter, as 
Trudy weakens and becomes increasingly influenced by the low-level 
steering flow, a turn toward the west-northwest is anticipated, 
taking the cyclone away from the coast early next week. The latest 
NHC track forecast has been adjusted slightly to the left of the 
previous prediction, toward the HCCA, GDMI, and TVCN consensus aids, 
but remains on the right side of the track guidance envelope, closer 
to the coast of Mexico.

Some additional strengthening is forecast during the next 24 h as 
Trudy moves over warmer waters with increasing ocean heat content, 
away from the relatively cool wakes of previous tropical cyclones. 
However, possible dry-air entrainment and the cyclone's increasing 
proximity to the coast of Mexico could limit strengthening. Beyond 
36 to 48 h, increasing southwesterly vertical wind shear and a 
progressively drier mid-level environment should induce steady 
weakening. These increasingly hostile conditions are expected to 
cause Trudy to lose its organized deep convection, with the cyclone 
forecast to become a post-tropical remnant low by day 4 and 
dissipate by day 5. The latest NHC intensity forecast is very 
similar to the previous prediction, but has been nudged slightly 
higher between 12 and 24 h to account for the recent improvement in 
Trudy's satellite presentation and the increasingly favorable 
oceanic conditions.

 
KEY MESSAGES:
 
1. Trudy is forecast to strengthen during the next 24 hours as it
approaches the coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico this
weekend, bringing an increasing risk of storm surge, damaging winds,
and flooding rain. Hurricane Warnings and Watches, as well as
Tropical Storm Warnings and Watches, are currently in effect for
portions of the coast, and additional watches and warnings may be
required.
 
2. Heavy rainfall associated with Trudy will impact the southwest
Mexican coast between Guerrero and Nayarit through the weekend. This
rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides along 
and near the southwest Mexican coast in Michoacán, Colima, and 
Jalisco, especially in areas along steep terrain.
 
3. Large swells are affecting portions of the coast of southwestern
Mexico and will spread northward through the weekend, causing
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions.
